body.statement: If \(\mathsf A_{\min}\) solves every rational instance of \(\operatorname{CompOpt}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell;g,r,c)\) in polynomial bit time, then one unconstrained call computes \(e^{\star}\), and at most \(\sum_{g=1}^{k}|R_g||K_g|\leq pq\) constrained calls compute every \(P_g(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell)\) and one attaining minimum completion for each retained pair. The resulting exact algorithm computes every \(S_{vu}(\widetilde W,\mathcal G,\ell)\), its common value when it is a singleton, and two attaining countermodels whenever it is not, using \(O(p^2q)\) additional rational operations; singletonness is checked directly by the zero and cross-multiplication comparisons in \(\text{prop:singleton-minor-corollary}\).
body.justification: The reduction separates the unresolved global optimization from polynomial image projection, equality checking, and witness extraction.
body.gap: IDA and lvLiNGAM certification exploit local graphical choices, whereas the mixed DOG projection requires global minimum-feasibility queries before local values can be trusted.
body.consumer: The reduction gives an implementation contract and prevents an effect-image routine from combining locally possible choices that never coexist in a minimum model.
